provisions.text: The entire territory of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is sacred and inviolable. Any actions that threaten national independence, unity, sovereignty, or territorial integrity, or that obstruct national defense and development, shall be severely punished.

The Lao People’s Democratic Republic conducts its foreign policy based on peace, independence, friendship, and cooperation. It seeks to expand relations and cooperation with all countries based on principles of peaceful coexistence, mutual respect for independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, non-interference in internal affairs, equality, and mutual benefit. The Lao PDR supports the struggles of peoples around the world for peace, national independence, democracy, and social progress.

National defense and public security are the responsibility, duty, and obligation of all organizations and every Lao citizen. The defense and security forces are the main pillars in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity; protecting the lives and property of the people; and ensuring the stability and sustainability of the people’s democratic regime. National defense and public security must be closely linked with socio-economic development and environmental protection.

Lao citizens have the right to personal safety and dignity, including life, body, reputation, and home. They may not be arbitrarily arrested, detained, or have their homes searched without a warrant from the public prosecutor or people’s court, except in cases specified by law.

The President is the Head of State of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, and represents the multiethnic Lao people both domestically and internationally. The President serves as the Chairman of the National Defense and Security Committee, and the Commander-in-Chief of the People’s Armed Forces. The President’s role is to guarantee the independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, stability, and security of the nation.

The President has the following rights and responsibilities: To promulgate the Constitution and laws; To issue presidential ordinances and decrees; To convene and preside over special meetings of the Government, and to participate in Standing Committee meetings of the National Assembly when necessary; To appoint, transfer, or dismiss the Deputy Prime Minister and members of the Government, after approval by the National Assembly; To appoint, transfer, or dismiss the Vice President of the Supreme People’s Court, the Vice President of the Supreme People’s Prosecutor Office, the Vice President of the State Inspection Authority, the Deputy Head of the Central Anti-Corruption Authority, and the Vice President of the State Audit Organization; To decide on the promotion, demotion or removal of military ranks within the national defense and security forces; To appoint, transfer, or dismiss the Head and Deputy Head of the Office of the President; To appoint or recall Ambassadors Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Lao PDR abroad, and to accept or reject foreign Ambassadors or Permanent Representatives accredited to Laos; To declare the formation of the national election commission, election dates, number of candidates, and seats for the National Assembly and provincial People’s Assemblies, based on proposals from the Standing Committee of the National Assembly; To declare war or peace based on the decision of the National Assembly; to approve general or partial mobilization and the state of emergency nationwide or in specific regions; To award or revoke national decorations such as Orders of Merit, Medals of Honor, Victory Medals, or other honorary titles; To grant pardons and declare amnesties, after approval by the National Assembly; To grant political asylum to foreign individuals. To decide on negotiations or signings, to declare ratification or accession, and to approve or terminate treaties in the name of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic.

The national emblem of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is circular. At the bottom, there is an image of half a cogwheel, above which is a red banner inscribed with the words: “Lao People’s Democratic Republic.” On both sides are stalks of fully ripe rice, forming a crescent shape. Another red banner across the middle bears the words: “Peace, Independence, Democracy, Unity, and Prosperity.” In the center of the circle are images of the That Luang stupa, a road, rice fields, forests, and a hydroelectric dam.

The national flag of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic has a blue field with red stripes on the top and bottom. A white moon is centered in the middle of the blue band. The height of the flag is two-thirds its length. Each red stripe is half the height of the blue band. The diameter of the white moon is four-fifths the height of the blue band.
The national anthem of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is the song titled “Pheng Xat Lao” (The Lao National Anthem).
